maml:description.maml:para: Plans and resumes a paced transfer of archive shards to an approved Git remote.

Revision 1.0.3. One self-contained Windows PowerShell 5.1 script. Requires Windows 10/11, installed Git for Windows 2.30 or newer, FullLanguage, and pre-provisioned credentials. Run as the current user. No installation, elevation, policy changes are performed. Git hooks, signing, credential helpers, TLS checks, and repository filters remain active.

Plan reads local repository information and writes a readable UTF-8 JSON document. It performs no network operation, staging, commit, or push. The document records SHA-256 hashes, exact Git blob IDs, the branch, the configured push destination's fingerprint, and a fixed wait for each pending file. Pacing is transparent and deterministic.

Push revalidates that document and processes one pending file at a time: verify -> add -> verify index -> commit -> verify commit -> push -> verify remote branch -> checkpoint. All shard sets must have contiguous numbering. Each matching checksum manifest is included after that set's shards. Legacy sets are accepted with a warning. This does not decrypt or test the archive. Already-identical files in the base commit need no new commit.

Push starts a 60-minute budget, persisted at <PlanPath>.state.json and <PlanPath>.start.json. The same Push command resumes automatically. Verified Git commits and the actual remote branch, rather than an optimistic counter, establish progress. One local commit may be awaiting push. Failed/uncertain pushes are not blindly retried. Last attempted/verified push times preserve pacing on resume. A timed-out plan remains inspectable but cannot restart its original budget. A completed checkpoint may be reverified later without sending more data. A new Plan is an explicit new transfer, with a new budget. Its base still must match the remote: resolve any pending older local commit through the approved Git recovery procedure before starting a replacement plan.

Completion within 60 minutes cannot be guaranteed: counts, bandwidth, authentication, hooks, server limits, and outages can make it impossible. Plan rejects waits consuming more than 50 minutes, reserving at least ten minutes for work. Push bounds Git calls and stops initiating work at its deadline. Blocking filesystem I/O and process cleanup can exceed the budget. Keep the Windows clock accurate. Fixed waiting starts after the previous attempt/verified completion; operation time adds to the planned waits.

The current branch must already exist remotely. At the first Push its remote tip must equal the plan's base commit, preventing upload of unrelated local commits. Divergence, branch changes, changed source bytes, and foreign staged changes cause a stop. Do not edit or use Git in this worktree during transfer. The exclusive sendshards.lock in Git's common directory serializes this tool across linked worktrees; it cannot lock out other Git applications.

Plan/state/logs must be outside the worktree and Git metadata. Plans contain private paths and file hashes and must be reviewed before sharing. Logs omit paths, remote URLs, payloads, credentials, raw Git output, and exception text. No success-stream result is produced. Files/shards are never removed. Failed commits can leave the next file staged; successful commits remain in Git. A verified, matching staged next file is accepted on resume. Rewriting history, resetting, stashing, force-pushing, and silently skipping hooks are not used. Hard termination can also leave a native Git index.lock; investigate native Git locks before resuming rather than deleting them while Git may still run. Use actual directory paths for plans/logs: directory symlink/junction ancestry is refused for these owned outputs so an external-looking path cannot redirect writes into the repository. Ordinary OneDrive cloud placeholders are not banned. Filters changing shard bytes (including LFS pointers) fail verification; use a repository configuration approved for preserving these file bytes.

Runtime limits: 10,000 shard/manifest files, 256 MiB per shard, 8 MiB per JSON document, 2 MiB captured output per native stream, 100 log files retained. Child executables: installed git.exe and its configured approved helpers/hooks; an in-file Windows Job Object adapter contains Git and its ordinary descendants from creation through cleanup, even after parent exit. No taskkill or uncontained fallback is used. No network contact occurs until an authorized Push.

The script may be installed under scripts/, in a repository root or in a separate tools directory and invoked from another directory. Relative CLI paths resolve from the caller’s PowerShell filesystem location. Source data stays in its Git worktree and plan/state/logs outside it. No XML or documentation is required to execute.

Revision 1.0.2 implements SS-01 and SS-02. Missing checkpoints with a surviving start record or exact transfer commits are refused; matching legacy checkpoints retain their original start. Keep plan/state/start records together. Git starts suspended in a kill-on-close Windows job using job-at-creation and explicit pipe inheritance. Cleanup uncertainty stops successful operations and retains primary failures. Real Windows Job Object, interruption and managed-endpoint acceptance remain NOT RUN; Linux protocol regressions use a development process-boundary adapter. See docs/sendshards/verification.md and operations.md.

Version 1.0.3 additionally rechecks the frozen repository, branch and push destination immediately before sending a commit, including changes made during commit hooks. Controlled use is an ordinary interactive user session with installed dependencies, local data and no concurrent repository/output writers. No elevation, installation, download or new network mechanism is added. Plan remains local; only Push contacts the configured remote using git push and git ls-remote, with approved Git helpers/hooks retained.
Generate a new plan. Existing plan, checkpoint or original-start files are never overwritten.
With Plan: a local folder inside the worktree, containing *.7z.NNN.txt shards. Top-level files only; multiple archive sets are supported. Other files ignored.
Required in either mode. JSON document outside the repository. Relative paths use the invocation's PowerShell filesystem location, not the script directory.
With Plan: configured remote name, default origin. Exactly one push URL required. The configured push URL is used for both push and remote verification.
With Plan: fixed minimum wait between pushes, default 30, range 5 through 600. This is a rate limit, not a means of avoiding security inspection.
With Plan: maximum duration of each Git command, default 60, range 10 through 300, further limited by the remaining execution budget.
Optional approved installed git.exe path. Otherwise resolved from PATH.
Execute or resume an existing plan. Repeating this command is the resume action.
None. Source files and the persisted plan are input data.
None on the success stream. Plan produces a JSON document. Push maintains a checkpoint and sanitized JSONL operational logs. Verbose/Debug use their streams.

maml:alert.maml:para: DOCUMENTATION PACKAGING, 12 OCTOBER 2026 Standalone execution requires no XML, Markdown or agent instruction files. Declared platform/application dependencies and runtime input/configuration still apply. The native .EXTERNALHELP directive is used only for detailed help. Without XML, native help falls back to generated parameter syntax. To retain detailed help, optionally deploy matching script/docs folders so ../docs/sendshards/sendshards-help.xml is available. Verification text below is historical; current extraction and standalone checks are recorded in docs/sendshards/verification.md.

WhatIf/declined confirmation: read-only local checks, no network, logs, locks, directories, staging, or checkpoint writes. Debug never introduces prompting. Exit: 0 complete/requested preview; 1 unexpected; 2 invalid input/plan; 3 operational/dependency/repository conflict; 4 controlled timeout. Binding, execution-policy refusal, Ctrl+C, and hard termination can occur outside this mapping. Missing completion is an unknown outcome; resume reconciles Git. Audit initialization must succeed before mutations. Later logging/cleanup failure warns without replacing the primary failure. Checkpoint failure stops further work. Normal retention removes only this tool's old log files, never plans/checkpoints.

Task Scheduler example (paths illustrative): Program: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe Arguments: -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File "C:\ApprovedTools\sendshards.ps1" -Push -PlanPath "C:\TransferPlans\batch.json" Start in: C:\ApprovedTools Use the intended user with approved network credentials; S4U lacks network access. Configure no overlapping instances, no automatic rapid retries, an execution limit above 60 minutes for cleanup, and suitable network/sleep/battery conditions. This script does not register tasks. External helpers/hooks can require prior setup; noninteractive PowerShell does not prevent every external application dialog.

Verification for revision 1.0.0: PASS: development-only native Git protocol checks on Linux, Git 2.51.1, Python 3.12: 11 asserted scenarios covering exact file/commit/remote bytes, manifest order, distinct fetch/push destinations, interrupted progress, Unicode/literal paths, hook rejection, filters, and wait-budget boundaries. These exercised native Git commands and a quoting model, NOT this script. PASS: lexical source checks (balanced strings/delimiters, unique functions, command-resolution inventory, prohibited-operation review), UTF-8 BOM. PASS: manual review of function size/control flow/nesting, source/index/commit guards, output suppression, and sanitized diagnostics. No AST metric claim. NOT RUN: PowerShell parser/PSScriptAnalyzer, target Windows PowerShell 5.1, Windows process/ACL behavior, Task Scheduler, endpoint/proxy/DLP acceptance. Those runtimes and the managed target environment are unavailable here.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION CLARIFICATIONS Use the same plan and persisted original budget to resume. Inspect Git locks and staged/local/remote state after interruption rather than deleting locks during live work or blindly retrying an uncertain push. Current Embelish shards contain no checksum manifest and are accepted with a legacy warning. No archive decryption or authenticity proof is performed. See docs/sendshards/operations.md and verification.md for current documentation and analyzer findings.

HISTORICAL AUDIT, 18 OCTOBER 2026 Version 1.0.0 had six findings (F1–F6); all are corrected in 1.0.1. Current verification on Linux/PowerShell 7.6.6: 68 functional scenarios pass using production functions and initial null deadlines, without a writer prototype. Saved-plan/checkpoint round trips, actual paced local transfer, completed/staged resume, malformed JSON/manifest/state types and root/scripts/external relocation are covered. All four scripts have zero parser/analyzer findings with the 5.1 compatibility profile, with narrowly documented helper exceptions. Windows runtime, owned process-tree cleanup, durability/production credentials/Scheduler and endpoint acceptance remain NOT RUN. See docs/sendshards/verification.md and the historical audit for details.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Repeat the same command after an interruption; no separate Resume flag is needed.
